summary:
Lunar Frontier: The Last 30 Days is a 3D survival and management simulation that puts the player in command of a four-person research outpost at the Lunar South Pole. Over a 30-day mission, the player keeps the crew alive by managing food, water, oxygen, and power. They assign astronauts to tasks based on skill, stamina, and morale. They also respond to emergencies such as solar storms, equipment failures, and spare-part shortages.

The project addresses the challenge of sustaining human life on the Moon by turning real constraints into decisions. These include closed-loop life support, lunar dust, radiation, limited resupply, and crew psychology. Resources are produced through connected systems rather than appearing automatically, so players learn why each system matters. Visible task execution, first-person and follow views, and a fair, telegraphed event system make those trade-offs easy to understand and engaging.

This matters because permanent lunar presence depends on planning, resource independence, and human factors as much as on engineering. Lunar Frontier makes these ideas accessible to students and the public, and it can serve as a foundation for education and research.
details:
Project Details: Lunar Frontier The Last 30 Days

What it does and how it works

Lunar Frontier is a 3D survival and management simulation. The player is the Mission Commander of a fourperson research outpost at the Lunar South Pole. Over a 30day mission, the player monitors food, water, oxygen, and power, decides what needs doing, and assigns the right astronaut to each task. The astronauts then walk to the building, do the work, and return, so every decision is visible.

Resources come from connected systems. Greenhouse crops grow over time, a recycler recovers water, a generator makes oxygen, and solar panels and batteries supply power. When power runs short, the player sets which systems get power first. Emergencies such as solar storms, equipment failures, illness, and spare part shortages come with warnings and offer several choices, each with a different cost. Players can watch from a strategy camera, a follow camera, or a first person helmet view. Collision keeps astronauts from passing through buildings.

Benefits

  • It turns real lunar constraints into decisions players can understand: closed loop life support, lunar dust, radiation, spacewalk limits, and crew morale.
  • Skills, stamina, and personalities make each astronaut’s role matter.
  • Task queues, auto assign, and suggestions keep a 30 day run from becoming tedious.
  • Difficulty levels and seeded random events give replay value.

Intended impact

A lasting presence on the Moon depends on planning, resource independence, and the human crew. We want players, especially students and the public, to learn why these matter by running a base themselves. We also see it as a base for classroom use and later research.

Tools and technology

  • TypeScript, with a deterministic simulation core that runs separately from the renderer
  • Three.js for 3D, React for the interface, and Rapier and a navmesh for movement and collision
  • Vitest and automated bot playthroughs for testing and balance
  • NASA’s CGI Moon Kit and NASA 3D Resources for lunar data and models, plus open-licensed assets
  • Claude, used for design, documentation, and coding-agent prompts

What is creative about it

The game combines strategy and simulation with first-person immersion. The player makes the decisions, and then sees them carried out through an astronaut’s helmet. Events are designed to be fair and understandable, and the Moon’s own problems drive the maintenance and the stories.

What we considered

  • Realism versus playability: we used simplified but plausible numbers.
  • Fairness: warnings come before events, and no situation is unwinnable.
  • Accessibility: colour-blind-safe design, text scaling, and motion options.
  • Performance: smooth cameras and stable frame rates.
  • Licensing and credit: every asset’s source and licence is recorded.
  • Testing: simulated playthroughs tune the balance and check for bugs.
